Replay

TURN relay tests with Coturn

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
RunningEvidence handling

These fixtures use Coturn and real Chrome peer connections. They force iceTransportPolicy: "relay", inspect the selected candidate pair through the browser's statistics API, and require relay candidates and transferred bytes on both sides. A successful direct localhost connection cannot satisfy the gate.

The relay binds only to 127.0.0.1. Test credentials are random and stored in a private work directory. The fixture deliberately permits loopback relay peers; that exception is for this local test and must not be copied to a public deployment. Neither these tests nor the library install a public relay or issue production relay credentials.

Running#

Provide a Coturn executable. Linux installations can use their packaged version. The repository's pinned Coturn derivation is marked broken on macOS; the fixture was tested using an isolated build of its pinned 4.9.0 source with existing native OpenSSL, libevent and SQLite development libraries:

Shell
COTURN_BUILD=/tmp/replay-coturn \
bash tests/replay_turn/build_coturn.sh

build_coturn.sh prints the executable path. It changes no system installation. COTURN_SOURCE supplies a pre-fetched source tree; otherwise Nix fetches the pinned source. COTURN_PREFIX defaults to /opt/local for the tested native setup.

Shell
TURNSERVER=/tmp/replay-coturn/bin/turnserver \
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_turn/run.sh

TURNSERVER=/tmp/replay-coturn/bin/turnserver REPLAY_PREBUILT=1 \
REPLAY_TURN_PROTOCOL=tcp \
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_turn/run.sh

TURNSERVER=/tmp/replay-coturn/bin/turnserver REPLAY_PREBUILT=1 \
REPLAY_TURN_SCENARIO=auth \
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_turn/run.sh

TURNSERVER=/tmp/replay-coturn/bin/turnserver REPLAY_PREBUILT=1 \
REPLAY_TURN_SCENARIO=outage \
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_turn/run.sh

TURNSERVER=/tmp/replay-coturn/bin/turnserver REPLAY_TURN_GAME=scrapyard \
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_turn/run.sh

TURNSERVER=/tmp/replay-coturn/bin/turnserver REPLAY_TURN_PROVIDER=1 \
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_turn/run.sh

Run these serially: the fixtures use relay ports 53000–53100. Cavecrawl is the default game; run its normal relay gate before the authentication scenario, which uses its built export. REPLAY_PREBUILT=1 requires current previously built game artifacts. Set REPLAY_TURN_OUT to retain results at a chosen path.

UDP/TCP selects the browser-to-TURN transport. Relayed peer traffic still uses the browser's WebRTC/DTLS data-channel stack. The selected candidate's relayProtocol must match the requested transport. The normal gates run menu enrollment, simultaneous-room isolation where included by the game fixture, gameplay, host migration and fresh-process rejoin. Scrapyard additionally checks the asset preparation barrier and active-combat checkpoint.

The authentication scenario gives the guest an intentionally wrong TURN password. It requires a candidate error, no connected candidate pair and no gameplay entry. A fresh process then uses correct ICE settings with the same stored membership, registers a newer incarnation and joins through the relay. This is not a general relay-outage/restart test.

The separate outage scenario retains the coordinator and game processes, stops and restarts the relay, and checks a new relay-selected connection, unchanged identity/epoch/inventory and a new authority-confirmed guest action. It requires the current Cavecrawl export. REPLAY_TURN_DOWNTIME_MS selects 1,000–30,000 ms of deliberate downtime before relay startup; actual downtime includes startup time. The same fixture can run with UDP or TCP relay transport. See RTC continuation for the reconnect mechanism.

Evidence handling#

The browser probe observes real constructors and calls getStats; it does not substitute peer connections, candidate pairs or payload traffic. Reports include candidate types, relay protocol and byte counters, omitting IPs and credentials. Coturn's verbose allocation/channel logs provide independent relay-side evidence. Never copy ice.json, turn.conf, credential databases or browser profiles into published results. Screenshots from the game fixtures mask party invite text.

Configuration validation runs independently:

Shell
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_turn/config_run.sh

It checks bounded ICE JSON, server/URL/credential structures, relay-only requirements, owned configuration strings and propagation into Room options, plus WASM compilation.

The authoritative contracts are Coturn's configuration, Godot's connection API, and the browser's selected-pair statistics. See recorded results for actual acceptance and the remaining public deployment limits.

The UDP datagram fault gate adds a bounded multi-client loopback proxy and Slopball planned/crash recovery checks under actual Chrome-to-TURN packet delay, loss and duplication.
